jurisdiction_body: New Hampshire Department of Energy (net metering rules En 900; interconnection rules to move to En 1000) and New Hampshire Public Utilities Commission (NEM tariffs/compensation, Puc 900 interconnection provisions)
rule_citation: RSA 362-A:9; En 900 (NH DOE net metering rules, eff 2026-04-27, replacing Puc 900 net-metering provisions); Puc 900 Parts 904-908 (small customer-generator <=100 kW interconnection, eff 2020-09-14); PUC Order 26,029 (DE 16-576, 2017-06-23, alternative/NEM 2.0 tariff); PUC Order 27,074 (DE 22-060, 2024-11-18, NEM 2.0 retained, application fees from 2025-01-01); Laws of 2026 Ch. 309 (HB 1718, approved 2026-07-10, storage in net metering, eff 2027-01-01)
applies_to: IOU + NHEC: the three PUC-regulated IOUs (Eversource/PSNH, Unitil, Liberty) plus New Hampshire Electric Cooperative (deregulated co-op; En 900 applies to it for standard-tariff customer-generators up to 3.16 MW and NHEC otherwise sets its own net-metering tariff). Municipal utilities (e.g. Littleton, Wolfeboro, Woodsville, Ashland, New Hampton) are not covered and set their own terms.
nem_successor: Alternative Net Metering tariff (NEM 2.0) for capacity allocations on/after 2017-09-01 (Order 26,029). Order 27,074 (DE 22-060, 2024-11-18) kept NEM 2.0 unchanged and kept the 2040-12-31 end of the legacy period (all net-metered customers move to then-current terms after Dec 2040). MID-TRANSITION: DE 22-060 Phase II (CPCNH Local Power Market) is open, and the 2024 settlement calls for the utilities to propose net-metering time-of-use rates about two years after the order (~late 2026). Pre-2017-09-01 customers are on the standard (full retail) tariff through 2040.
nem_cap_nonres_kw: 1000 (large customer-generator >100 kW to 1 MW AC; municipal host/political subdivision up to 5000 kW)
nem_aggregate_cap: No aggregate MW cap stated for the alternative (NEM 2.0) tariff in En 900 / Puc 900. The MW caps in Puc 903.02(b) apply only to the legacy standard tariff (Liberty 8.74 MW, NHEC 3.16 MW, Eversource 75.38 MW, Unitil 12.72 MW) and are closed.
nem_sizing_rule: No %-of-load sizing rule for small generators. The facility must be behind the meter and used to offset the customer's own requirements. Large (>100 kW) customer-generators on NEM 2.0 must consume at least 20% of annual generation behind the meter unless registered as a group host (En 903.02(b)).
export_credit_value: Small (<=100 kW) on NEM 2.0: net excess kWh credited at 100% default energy service + 100% transmission + 25% distribution per-kWh charges; competitive-supply customers get only the transmission + 25% distribution part. Non-bypassable charges (SBC, stranded cost, storm recovery, consumption tax) are billed on gross imports. Large (>100 kW): credited at the default energy service rate only, and all kWh charges apply to gross imports. LMI community solar group adder applies separately. Rates vary with semi-annual default service.
credit_rollover: indefinite (monetary bill credit carried forward); cash-out by check optional once a year if the balance is >=$100 after the March cycle (alternative tariff), or on account closure
annual_true_up: March billing cycle: utility notifies by June 1 anyone holding credits >=$100 (NEM 2.0) or a surplus >600 kWh (legacy standard tariff); the customer may elect a check, otherwise credits roll forward (En 903.02(f)-(g)). Group hosts get an annual true-up by July 1: exports above group load are re-priced at avoided cost.
ic_standard: IEEE 1547-2018 or UL 1741 SA (Puc 906.01). IOUs apply ISO-NE Source Requirement Document ride-through (UL 1741 SA grid-support inverter) since 2018-06-01.
ic_fast_track_kw: 1000 kW export capacity under En 1000 (NH DOE DER interconnection rules, adopted 2026-07-17; effective date not confirmed). Fast track has a 25-business-day screen, and the simplified process covers certified inverter-based <=50 kW nameplate / <=25 kW export. Until En 1000 takes effect, Puc 900 has no fast-track tier.
ic_simplified_kw: 100 (Puc 904-908 simplified inverter process for small customer-generators <=100 kW; >100 kW handled under each utility's own interconnection tariff/guidelines)
ic_application_fee: IOU fee schedule per the DE 22-060 settlement adopted by Order 27,074, from 2025-01-01: $200 up to 25 kW, $500 for 25-100 kW, $1,000 over 100 kW. Plus a $500 non-refundable pre-application fee for >100 kW/non-inverter projects (Eversource). Engineering review costs apply above 10 kW and for non-inverter systems.
ic_study_trigger_kw: Feeder studies may be required when aggregate DG on the feeder reaches the lower of 7.5% of peak feeder demand at the substation or 20% of peak demand downstream of the POI, or when more than one net-metered facility shares a secondary (Puc 905.06). Above 100 kW, per utility tariff.
external_disconnect: Waived for inverter-based: not required for a compliant single- or 3-phase inverter unless the revenue meter is not routinely accessible, inverters are in series, or service is transformer-rated (Puc 905.01)
insurance_required: None: utilities and suppliers may not require property or personal liability insurance (Puc 904.07). A mutual indemnity agreement applies unless both parties waive it (Puc 904.03).
ic_timeline_days: Completeness notice within 10 business days (Puc 904.04). Witness test attempted within 10 business days of the certificate of completion; witness test required above 10 kW unless waived. Eversource says approved applications typically come back in under a week.
grid_charging_allowed: Requires non-export (from 2027-01-01): Laws 2026 Ch. 309 (HB 1718) amends RSA 362-A:1-a II-b and adds RSA 362-A:9 XXIV/XXV. Storage configured to export must charge only from the on-site net-metered generation, unless charging is controlled by an entity other than the customer-generator (e.g. utility/aggregator dispatch) or the PUC authorizes otherwise in an adjudicated proceeding. PUC to set compensation terms for storage exports. Before 2027-01-01 there is no explicit statewide rule: Unclear.
non_export_option: No statewide non-export/limited-export path defined in Puc 900/En 900. Ch. 309 implies a non-exporting battery may grid-charge. DOE is directed to adopt storage installation/interconnection rules (RSA 374-H:2 as amended, eff 2027-01-01).
storage_counts_toward_cap: No from 2027-01-01: Ch. 309 says energy storage may be added to a net-metered generation facility without affecting its size determination for net-metering eligibility. Currently, the NEM cap is measured on the generator's inverter AC rating (En 902.18); storage treatment before 2027 is not explicit.

rule_citation: 30 V.S.A. § 8010; PUC Rule 5.100 (Net-Metering, revised eff 2024-03-01); PUC Rule 5.500 (Interconnection Procedures for Generation Resources and Energy Storage Devices, revised 2024-03-01); 2026 Biennial Update, Case 26-0291-INV (new blended rate and adjustors eff 2026-08-01)
applies_to: All utilities: Rule 5.100 applies to every Vermont electric company, including municipals (e.g. Burlington Electric) and co-ops (VEC, WEC). Each company files a compliance net-metering tariff under Rule 5.134/5.128.
nem_successor: Rule 5.100 (2017 overhaul, revised 2024-03-01): excess generation is monetized at the utility's blended residential rate. Separate per-kWh REC and siting adjustors apply to all production-meter kWh. They are fixed in each system's CPG and reset every two years for new systems (biennial update). Zero or positive adjustors last 10 years; negative adjustors apply in perpetuity. Pre-2017 systems follow only the listed legacy provisions (5.125(H)). MID-TRANSITION: the 2026 biennial update (Case 26-0291-INV) set new values for CPG applications filed on/after 2026-08-01.
nem_cap_res_kw: 500 (kW AC inverter nameplate for PV; Category I <=15 kW; Category II >15-150 kW preferred site; Category III >150-500 kW preferred site; Category IV >15-500 kW non-preferred site)
nem_aggregate_cap: No statewide MW aggregate cap. Instead, a 500 kW cumulative limit applies per customer/group allocation (5.129(D)). Utilities may propose locational adjustor fees for constrained or limited-headroom areas (5.136).
nem_sizing_rule: Net-metering system must primarily serve on-site/group load; no %-of-load cap found in Rule 5.100 beyond the 500 kW per-customer limit
export_credit_value: Blended residential rate: $0.2071/kWh statewide, eff 2026-08-01 (was $0.18398 since 2024), per the 2026 biennial update. Some utilities' own blended rates may be lower (5.127(A) uses the lowest of the options). REC adjustor: $0.00 if RECs are transferred to the utility, -$0.04/kWh if retained. Siting adjustors for new CPG applications filed on/after 2026-08-01: Cat I -$0.05, Cat II -$0.05, Cat III -$0.07, Cat IV -$0.08/kWh (verified against the Case 26-0291-INV order of 2026-05-29, ordering paragraphs 1-7. The order cuts Cat I/II siting from -$0.04 to -$0.05, while Cat III/IV are unchanged. Net new-system compensation, Cat I/II with RECs transferred, is about $0.1571/kWh).
credit_rollover: 12-month expiry: accumulated bill credit must be used within 12 months of the month earned or it reverts to the utility without compensation (5.129(B))
ic_standard: IEEE 1547 series + UL 1741 as adopted (Rule 5.500 §5.520, revised 2024-03-01). A superseding revision applies to applications filed more than 6 months after the revision date. Export settings reference IEEE 1547-2018 Table 28. Application forms were revised in Case 26-0673-INV (order 2026-05-28).
ic_fast_track_kw: 500 (Rule 5.510 procedure for nameplate <=500 kW. Projects with export <=15 kW and nameplate <=50 kW get only 3 simple screens. Projects >500 kW follow §5.511 plus the §5.512 Preliminary Review screens.)
ic_simplified_kw: 15 (systems <=15 kW: the Rule 5.100 registration form doubles as the Rule 5.500 interconnection application, 5.105(B)(1))
ic_application_fee: No fee for nameplate <=150 kW unless an approved utility tariff sets one. >150 kW (generation + storage combined): $600 or the tariff amount, non-refundable after 7 days. Optional pre-application report: $300 (Rule 5.502(3), (36)).
ic_study_trigger_kw: No fixed kW trigger: feasibility, system-impact and facilities studies are required only when a project fails the Preliminary Review screens (§5.512-5.515). Projects >1 MW are forwarded to VELCO/ISO-NE for review (§5.508).
external_disconnect: Not addressed: no utility-accessible disconnect-switch requirement found in Rule 5.500. May be set by utility interconnection requirements.
insurance_required: Not addressed: no insurance provision found in Rule 5.500
ic_timeline_days: Nameplate <=500 kW: incompleteness notice within 7 days. Issues must be flagged by day 15 (export <=15 kW) or day 31 (export >15-500 kW) after a complete application (§5.510). >500 kW: completeness within 14 days, then Preliminary Review 30 days. An IA is issued within 7 days after passing, and projects <150 kW without operating restrictions need no IA (§5.512).
grid_charging_allowed: Yes-but-not-credited: Rule 5.137 requires storage connected to a net-metering system to be configured so the customer cannot receive net-metering compensation for electricity drawn from any source other than the net-metering system. Utilities may not interconnect storage in a way that lets non-NM electricity earn NM credit. So grid charging is not prohibited, but grid-charged energy that is exported earns no net-metering credit. 5.137 also applies to pre-existing (pre-2017) systems.
non_export_option: Yes: Rule 5.522 lists Limited-Export and Non-Exporting methods (reverse-power, minimum-power and directional-power relays, UL 1741-certified power control systems, and mutually agreed means including paired solar+storage). Studies use Export Capacity, not nameplate (§5.503(A)). The utility may impose storage inverter settings or operating regimes (§5.503(B)).
storage_counts_toward_cap: No: 'capacity' for solar is the aggregate AC nameplate of the inverters used to convert the plant's output (Rule 5.100 definitions). Storage is not listed as counting. Not explicitly addressed for DC-coupled hybrid inverters.

rule_citation: 35-A M.R.S. §3209-A (NEB kWh credit) and §3209-B (NEB tariff rate); MPUC Rule Ch. 313 (Customer Net Energy Billing); MPUC Rule Ch. 324 (Small Generator Interconnection Procedures, as amended in Docket 2023-00103, order 2023-11-03); MPUC Advisory Ruling, Docket 2020-00332 (Feb 2021, storage paired with NEB); PL 2023 c. 411 (LD 1986); PL 2025 c. 430 (LD 1777, eff 2025-09-24); tariff-rate orders of 2025-12-17 in Dockets 2019-00197 and 2022-00185
applies_to: All utilities: Ch. 313 and Ch. 324 apply to every T&D utility (IOUs CMP and Versant, plus consumer-owned utilities). Consumer-owned utilities may cap NEB facilities at 100 kW unless they opt to allow up to <5 MW, may limit accounts to 10, and need not offer shared NEB (Ch. 313 §3(C)(4) and §3(E)).
nem_successor: No successor for behind-the-meter NEB. The OPA says LD 1777 left rooftop NEB unchanged. Front-of-meter changes: after 2025-12-31 no new NEB agreements for DG interconnected on the utility side of the meter (§3209-A(10)-(11)). Amendments after 2025-06-01 may not extend the delivery-period end date (§3209-A(2-A)). LD 1777 also added a monthly NEB project charge on larger DG and ended indexing of tariff-rate credits to future rate increases. Non-residential customers can instead choose the NEB tariff-rate (dollar credit) program; rates are set through 2046 by the 2025-12-17 orders. MID-TRANSITION: enforcement of parts of LD 1777 was delayed during federal-court litigation (Dec 2025, Foley Hoag, Secondary); status not verified.
nem_cap_res_kw: <5000 kW AC nameplate by statute. In practice new facilities must be <1000 kW, because 1-2 MW and 2-5 MW facilities qualify only if they met COD/agreement deadlines that ended 2024-12-31 (§3209-A(7) and (9)). Consumer-owned utilities: 100 kW unless the utility opts higher.
nem_cap_nonres_kw: <5000 kW (same statutory limits; effectively <1000 kW for new facilities; municipal-customer exception allows larger nameplate if <5 MW is used for NEB)
nem_aggregate_cap: No statewide MW cap for NEB. The 750 MW goal for 2-5 MW projects was exceeded (OPA: more than 1,600 MW built). A utility must notify the PUC when NEB capacity reaches 10% of its peak demand (Ch. 313 §3(P)(1)).
nem_sizing_rule: No %-of-load sizing limit found in Ch. 313. The facility must be used primarily to offset the customer's own bills (CMP CNEBA Art. II). LD 1777 requires community-solar subscription sizes to match customer usage.
export_credit_value: kWh credit: 1:1 offset of kWh-based charges only (supply and volumetric delivery). Fixed and non-kWh charges still apply (Ch. 313 §3(J)(4)). Tariff rate (non-residential): standard offer plus 75% of the effective T&D rate of the smallest commercial class for pre-reform projects. CY2025 Original Tariff Rate, small commercial: CMP $0.204101/kWh, Versant BHD $0.220136, Versant MPD $0.224619. Rates for 2026-2046 are in the 2025-12-17 order attachments (not read).
credit_rollover: annual expiry: rolling 12-month. Unused kWh or dollar credits expire 12 months after they are earned, with no compensation. Utilities remit the value of expired kWh credits to low-income assistance programs (§3209-A(8)).
annual_true_up: None: rolling 12-month expiry, no annual cash-out
ic_standard: IEEE 1547 + UL 1741 (Ch. 324 §5; the rule text does not name an edition). Equipment must be NRTL-listed.
ic_fast_track_kw: 25 (Level 1: certified inverter-based <=25 kW, with default approval if the utility does not act within 20 business days)
ic_simplified_kw: 2000 (Level 2 screens for certified generators <=2 MW; the On-Site-Load ICGF sub-tier covers 25-250 kW. Level 3 covers non-exporting facilities <=10 MW)
ic_application_fee: Level 1: $100 application plus $150 cost-sharing fee (covers upgrades up to $5,000). Level 2: $100 + $2/kW. On-Site-Load ICGF 25-250 kW: plus $25/kW cost-sharing fee (covers upgrades up to $10,000). Level 3 (non-exporting): $100 + $3/kW. Level 4: $3,000 plus study time, and $500 per application change. Engineering review: $100/hr (Ch. 324 §§3, 11-15).
ic_study_trigger_kw: 2000 (Level 4 feasibility/impact/facilities studies apply to exporting facilities >2 MW, to non-exporting facilities >10 MW, and to any facility that fails Level 1-3 screens)
external_disconnect: Not required: a utility may not require a utility-accessible disconnect switch, extra tests or extra insurance for an ICGF that meets the Ch. 324 §5 standards, unless the applicant agrees (Ch. 324 §15(E))
insurance_required: Inverter-based: none <=1 MW; $1M for >2-5 MW; $2M for >5 MW. Non-inverter: none <=50 kW; $500k for 50-500 kW; $1M for 500 kW-2 MW; $2M for 2-5 MW; $3M for >5 MW (Ch. 324 §15(F), at utility option)
ic_timeline_days: Level 1: 5 business days (BD) completeness check, 10 BD screens, deemed approved at 20 BD. Level 2: 5 BD completeness, 15 BD screens, then 10 BD to send IA. Level 3: 17 BD screens. Level 4: impact and facilities studies 45 BD each.
grid_charging_allowed: Requires non-export: under the MPUC Advisory Ruling (Docket 2020-00332), a battery paired with an NEB facility needs controls that stop it charging from the grid. If it can grid-charge, controls must stop it discharging to the grid. Facilities >100 kW with storage must file a yearly attestation. Removing the controls ends NEB eligibility and credits can be clawed back (CMP and Versant NEB agreements/applications). Ch. 324 §10 requires an ESS form stating the charging mode (grid only / unrestricted / restricted / ICGF only).
non_export_option: Yes: Ch. 324 §8 lists acceptable export-control methods (reverse-power 32R, minimum-power 32F, directional-power 32, UL 1741-certified Power Control Systems) for Non-Exporting and Limited-Export ICGFs. Level 3 is an expedited path for non-exporting facilities <=10 MW.
storage_counts_toward_cap: Unclear: NEB size limits apply to generator nameplate (AC). No rule text found on whether paired ESS kW counts. Ch. 324 uses Export Capacity (net of export controls) for screening.
